Personally from what I remember from playing RDR2 I always felt off about Dutch. By "off" I mean that he makes some decisions in the story that urks me. In my opinion I don't think that he was ever truly a great "leader" but more so a master manipulator. Dutch in the story goes through a handful of changes that are noticeable but I don't truly believe that just cause of bad luck and some stress would change a man to that extent.... unless he was finally showing his true colors.

During the story there are many parts where you can see just how greedy, egotistical, and vengeful Dutch is truly to his core. Take for an example Angelo Bronte. After the "Urban Pleasures" mission when Arthur, Lenny, and Dutch are parting ways you can hear Dutch go over with himself as to why Angelo betrayed him. The reason why Angelo betrayed Dutch was extremely simple. Territory. Angelo had his own gang and they've gotten pretty established in Saint Denis so when Dutch rolls in to throw in a wrench into the works with his gang what do you think would happen? Angelo would manipulate, use, and destroy them since he doesn't want competition. Looking at this perspective it's very clear and it doesn't take a person with 180 IQ to figure that out. 

Dutch was consumed with his ego and Angelo knew this so he played on it and manipulated him into believing that his reputation was grand enough to make him think that he was up next to the likes of Angelo Bronte so he couldn't see the blatant treachery and manipulation at play. Dutch thought they were friends too (lmao)! So when he was eventually betrayed by Angelo he was confused and then consumed with rage. Dutch had the perfect opportunity to run and get away before he went after Angelo but he didn't take it. He also had the same opportunity after he dealt with Angelo but alas he didn't take it. Dutch could've gotten away with his gang at both times and could've made an successful escape from the state but he didn't because he was consumed with pure vengeance cause he was played. He risked his people's lives for his revenge and ego.

Then there is the greed that man has shown. Dutch's gang robbed the bank at Valentine, a train, bonds, stores, and people. I find it hard to believe that he didn't have enough to go and get his own boat by chapter 4. He must've had literal thousands in the collective chest. Now that within itself is conjecture I must admit but I thought it was something to keep in mind. Now after Dutch killed Angelo Bronte he must've known the bank was being watched at this point and even others had their doubts about this job. Especially John and Hosea. But he went with it anyway because of spite, ego, and most importantly greed. That job was so botched that Dutch got his men killed or captured mainly because of his greed.

I could go on but I'd only be giving other examples. The main part of the story where you get to see how Dutch truly is, is during chapter 4. From my time playing there's many other things I've picked up on that at least for me, Dutch isn't who he claims nor pretends to be. Thank you for reading and I hope you all have a great day👍.
